title: Function binding JSON validator and edge-case guidance
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary: Implement a focused JSON-schema based validator and runtime compatibility layer for function/tool bindings. Scope includes the on-disk & API schema format, strict/lenient validation modes, a structured error taxonomy for surfaceable messages, and migration rules for legacy tool manifests. Goal is to reduce operational incidents from malformed tool calls and to provide deterministic error messages that guide SDKs and calling applications to automatically repair or surface minimal guidance to end-users.

Why now: Several recent incidents (see attachments) involved ambiguous tool parameter errors that caused silent failures or hard-to-parse assistant responses. We need a small, well-documented validation surface that: 1) fits into streaming/generation flows without large latency impact, 2) supports backward-compatible schema relaxation for older manifests, and 3) provides machine-readable error codes for telemetry and SDK mapping.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A JSON schema representation format documented in Confluence and included in the runtime schema registry.
2) A validator library integrated into the request flow that supports strict and lenient modes toggled per-route.
3) Error messages follow the new taxonomy with stable machine codes (ERR_BINDING_XXX) and user-friendly summary text.
4) Integration tests covering happy path, missing required param, type coercion, unknown-field warnings, and array shape edge cases.
5) A rollout plan that enables opt-in via a feature flag and telemetry to measure false positives/blocked calls.
design_decisions:
- Use a compact JSON-schema subset (types: string, number, boolean, array, object; union via 'oneOf' discouraged) to keep validator fast and deterministic.
- Provide 'coercion hints' field on params for controlled type coercion (e.g., allow-string-to-number) instead of implicit coercion in runtime.
- Introduce a per-parameter 'compatibility' field with values 'strict'|'compat'|'deprecated' to encode migration intent.
- Validation modes: 'strict' returns error on any mismatch; 'lenient' emits structured warnings and attempts safe coercions when allowed.
- Keep schema format extensible via top-level 'x-meta' freeform map for downstream tooling; runtime ignores unknown x-meta keys rather than failing.
validation_rules:
- Required fields must be present and non-null in strict mode.
- Types must match; if coercion hint exists and mode=lenient, apply explicit coercion rules and emit WARN_BINDING_COERCION.
- Unknown fields: in strict mode, ERR_BINDING_UNKNOWN_FIELD; in lenient mode, WARN_BINDING_IGNORED_FIELD.
- Arrays: validate element shapes; if heterogeneous arrays detected, return ERR_BINDING_ARRAY_SHAPE.
- Nested objects: recursion depth capped (default 6) to protect streaming memory.
- Size limits: total serialized params must not exceed 64KB by default (route-configurable).
- Function IDs: resolver validates binding to registered function manifest; missing manifest => ERR_BINDING_NO_MANIFEST with link to guidance.
error_taxonomy:
- ERR_BINDING_MISSING_REQUIRED: required parameter missing.
- ERR_BINDING_TYPE_MISMATCH: parameter had wrong type and coercion not allowed.
- ERR_BINDING_COERCION_APPLIED: coercion applied (warning code).
- ERR_BINDING_UNKNOWN_FIELD: strict mode rejected unknown param.
- ERR_BINDING_ARRAY_SHAPE: array element types/shapes inconsistent.
- ERR_BINDING_SIZE_EXCEEDED: params exceed configured byte limit.
- ERR_BINDING_NO_MANIFEST: manifest not found for function id.
- ERR_BINDING_DEPRECATED_PARAM: parameter marked deprecated; warning emitted with migration suggestion.
Each error includes: machine_code (above), human_message short text, path (json-path string), and remediation_hint string. These must be serializable as flat fields on the runtime error envelope for SDK mapping.
telemetry_and_alerting:
- Track validation outcome counts by route/model/tenant: success, coercion-warn, blocked-error.
- Record distribution of ERR_* codes for triage dashboards.
- Create an alert for spikes in ERR_BINDING_NO_MANIFEST and ERR_BINDING_SIZE_EXCEEDED (pager P1).
- Add sample payload capture (scrubbed) for top error types to aid debugging, stored for 7 days.
- Expose per-route false-positive rate when lenient-mode coerces successfully; use for migration rollouts.
rollout_plan: 1) Initial implementation behind 'binding-validator' feature flag at runtime and SDK opt-in. 2) Internal dogfood: enable lenient mode for 10 internal teams for 2 weeks and collect telemetry. 3) Flip default to lenient for new routes while exposing strict as an opt-in knob in route config. 4) After stability period and <1% false positive rate, flip stricter checks on for high-security customers via Dedicated/Private profiles. 5) Document migration patterns and publish SDK helpers to automatically adjust parameter shapes.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for each validation rule and error code.
- Integration tests: validate end-to-end tool call flows in streaming generation (simulate partial stream + validation failure mid-stream).
- Performance tests: measure added latency on 99th percentile token emission in streaming path (target <2ms overhead per call).
- Fuzz tests: random manifests and inputs to surface edge cases (array depth, recursion, unexpected data types).
- Back-compat tests: ensure legacy manifests with 'compat' flags still accept common inputs in lenient mode.
open_questions:
- Should the runtime auto-truncate overly large string params when size exceeds limit, or always return ERR_BINDING_SIZE_EXCEEDED? (UX vs safety trade-off)
- Naming: prefer WARN_BINDING_* or INFO_BINDING_* for non-blocking issues? Consensus lean towards WARN_BINDING_*.
- Do we accept 'oneOf' unions for complex param shapes or encourage a discriminated union pattern instead?
- How to expose remediation hints without leaking internal implementation details?
Responses needed from PM and Security before we finalize schema extension points.

2026-03-11 Security (Hannah L.): Agrees with x-meta ignore strategy but requests that remediation_hint never include internal endpoints. Added to security checklist.

2026-03-13 QA (Lena T.): Found two streaming integration edge cases where validation triggers after initial tokens are emitted; proposed approach to pre-validate blocking parameters before starting stream.
